runbook.subject: service reliability and operations runbook
runbook.latency_and_error_budget_monitoring: Dashboards track p50, p95, and p99 latency alongside error budgets, with latency budgets allocated per hop.
runbook.error_budget_review_cadence: Error budgets are reviewed weekly in the reliability meeting.
runbook.dependency_management: Dependencies are declared in the service manifest, validated at deploy time, pinned, and upgraded through automated pull requests.
runbook.deployment_controls: Deploys use the standard pipeline and require a green build, while canaries receive 5% of traffic for 30 minutes before promotion.
runbook.configuration_and_schema_change_controls: Configuration changes are peer reviewed and applied through the deployment tool, and schema changes use expand-and-contract migrations.
runbook.staging_and_load_testing: Staging mirrors production topology at one-tenth scale, with nightly load tests run against it.
runbook.request_safety_controls: Mutating endpoints require idempotency keys, requests propagate correlation IDs downstream, and gateway rate limiting uses a per-client token bucket.
runbook.health_check_interval: Readiness endpoint health checks run every 10 seconds.
runbook.observability_pipeline: Structured logs include request path, status code, and duration; logs are retained for 30 days, and metrics are exported every 15 seconds.
runbook.synthetic_monitoring: Synthetic probes exercise critical user journeys every minute.
runbook.resilience_mechanisms: Circuit breakers open after five consecutive downstream failures, retries use exponential backoff with jitter, cached responses provide graceful degradation, and graceful shutdown drains in-flight requests.
runbook.capacity_and_resource_management: Connection pools follow the downstream capacity model, garbage-collection pauses indicate memory pressure, and capacity planning is revisited quarterly.
runbook.backup_and_recovery: Backups run daily and are verified weekly by restoring them to a scratch cluster; long-running jobs checkpoint progress for restart recovery.
runbook.security_and_access_controls: Traffic uses mutual TLS, production access is just-in-time and audited, container images are scanned before promotion, and secrets rotate every 90 days.
runbook.operational_ownership_and_reviews: The runbook is reviewed quarterly by the owning team, engineers rotate through support weekly, post-incident reviews are blameless and published, and cost reports are reviewed monthly with finance.

runbook.observability: Metrics are exported every 15 seconds; logs capture request path, status code, and duration; logs are retained for 30 days; dashboards show p50, p95, and p99 latency with error budgets.
runbook.health_monitoring: Readiness checks run every 10 seconds, synthetic probes exercise critical user journeys every minute, and garbage-collection pauses indicate memory pressure.
runbook.reliability_controls: The service uses graceful shutdown, cached-response degradation, exponential-backoff retries with jitter, circuit breakers after five consecutive downstream failures, and checkpointing for resumable long-running jobs.
runbook.traffic_protection: Gateway rate limiting uses a per-client token bucket, and idempotency keys are required for all mutating endpoints.
runbook.capacity_management: Connection pools follow the downstream capacity model, latency budgets are allocated per hop, and capacity planning is revisited quarterly.
runbook.deployment_process: Deploys use the standard pipeline with a green-build requirement, while canary releases expose 5% of traffic for 30 minutes before promotion.
runbook.release_safety: Feature flags are managed through the configuration service with gradual rollout, and schema changes use expand-and-contract migrations.
runbook.dependency_management: Dependencies are declared in the service manifest, validated at deployment, and pinned and upgraded through automated pull requests.
runbook.security_controls: Container images are vulnerability-scanned before promotion, production access is just-in-time and audited, and service traffic uses mutual TLS.
runbook.secret_management: Secrets are rotated automatically every 90 days.
runbook.configuration_management: Configuration changes require peer review and are applied through the deployment tool.
runbook.backup_recovery: Backups run daily and are verified weekly by restoring them to a scratch cluster.
runbook.testing_environment: Nightly load tests run against staging, whose production topology is mirrored at one-tenth scale.
runbook.operations_governance: Engineers rotate through support weekly; alerts follow the paging escalation policy; the on-call handbook documents escalation and response times; runbooks are reviewed quarterly; post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.

changelog.previous_owner: Person or team that owned the service before the change.
changelog.current_on_call: Person assigned to primary on-call after the change.
changelog.previous_on_call: Person assigned to primary on-call before the change.
changelog.source_region: Cloud or deployment region from which the service was migrated.
changelog.destination_region: Cloud or deployment region to which the service was migrated.
changelog.numeric_policy_value: Numeric value explicitly stated for an operational policy, such as traffic percentage, duration, retention days, or failure threshold.
changelog.numeric_policy_unit: Unit associated with the numeric policy value, such as percent, minutes, days, or failures.
changelog.operational_practices: Flat list of concrete operational practices, controls, dependencies, schedules, or decisions stated in the change record.
